# gogo bytecode reference

<!-- Generated by tools/bcdoc from runtime/vm/opcodes.h and runtime/vm/image.h. Do not edit:
     edit the structured comments in opcodes.h and run `make bytecode-doc`. -->

This is the per-opcode reference for the gogo VM, generated from the single source of truth,
`runtime/vm/opcodes.h` (the Go compiler parses the same file, `compiler/opcodes.go` mirrors it and
`TestOpcodesMatchC` keeps the two equal). The design behind it is in [design.md](design.md) §5.6
(bytecode, image layout, versioning) and §5.5 (value representation); `gogo dis file.ggb` prints a
program's bytecode. Image format 15.6.

## Instruction encoding

An instruction is one little-endian 32-bit word: `op | a<<8 | b<<16 | c<<24` (opcode in the low
byte, then three 8-bit operands). Ops marked **+ext** are followed by one extra 32-bit word, `ext`,
which is not decoded as an instruction (a jump may land on it, so it is checked when used).
The VM is register-based: `ra`, `rb`, `rc` are the registers numbered by operands `a`, `b`, `c` in the
current frame; there is no operand stack, so "effect" is register notation. Function indexes, type
ids and jump targets (absolute code word indexes) are checked when used, and an out-of-range one is
`badcode` (the actor crashes with `R_BAD_CODE`).

## Opcodes

| # | Name | Operands | Ext | Effect | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | `OP_NOP` | - |  | - | Do nothing. |
| 1 | `OP_MOVE` | `a=dst b=src` |  | `ra = rb` | Copy a register. |
| 2 | `OP_LOADK` | `a=dst ext=term` | +ext | `ra = ext` | Load a raw term: small int, special immediate or constant-area ref (checked against the const map when executed). |
| 3 | `OP_LOADI32` | `a=dst ext=int32` | +ext | `ra = int32(ext)` | Load a 32-bit integer, boxed as an int64 when it does not fit an immediate. |
| 4 | `OP_ADD` | `a=dst b=lhs c=rhs` |  | `ra = rb + rc` | int addition (int only; int64 is ADD64). |
| 5 | `OP_SUB` | `a=dst b=lhs c=rhs` |  | `ra = rb - rc` | int subtraction. |
| 6 | `OP_MUL` | `a=dst b=lhs c=rhs` |  | `ra = rb * rc` | int multiplication. |
| 7 | `OP_DIV` | `a=dst b=lhs c=rhs` |  | `ra = rb / rc` | int division, truncated; a zero divisor crashes with R_DIV_ZERO. |
| 8 | `OP_REM` | `a=dst b=lhs c=rhs` |  | `ra = rb % rc` | int remainder; a zero divisor crashes with R_DIV_ZERO. |
| 9 | `OP_NEG` | `a=dst b=src` |  | `ra = -rb` | int negation. |
| 10 | `OP_EQ` | `a=dst b=lhs c=rhs` |  | `ra = rb == rc` | Equality of ints, bools, strings (by content), PIDs and Refs; an int64 box is badcode (use EQ64). |
| 11 | `OP_NE` | `a=dst b=lhs c=rhs` |  | `ra = rb != rc` | Inequality, as EQ. |
| 12 | `OP_LT` | `a=dst b=lhs c=rhs` |  | `ra = rb < rc` | int less-than. |
| 13 | `OP_LE` | `a=dst b=lhs c=rhs` |  | `ra = rb <= rc` | int less-or-equal. |
| 14 | `OP_NOT` | `a=dst b=src` |  | `ra = !rb` | Boolean negation. |
| 15 | `OP_JMP` | `ext=target` | +ext | `pc = code + ext` | Unconditional jump to an absolute code word index. |
| 16 | `OP_JMPF` | `a=cond ext=target` | +ext | `if !ra: pc = code + ext` | Jump if ra is false. |
| 17 | `OP_JMPT` | `a=cond ext=target` | +ext | `if ra: pc = code + ext` | Jump if ra is true. |
| 18 | `OP_CALL` | `a=dst b=args c=nargs ext=func` | +ext | `ra = func ext(rb .. rb+c-1)` | Call a function by index; c must equal its parameter count. The result returns into ra via RET or RETN. |
| 19 | `OP_RET` | `a=src` |  | `return ra` | Return one value into the caller's CALL or CALLV destination register. |
| 20 | `OP_NEWSTRUCT` | `a=dst b=fields c=nfields ext=type` | +ext | `ra = struct ext{rb .. rb+c-1}` | Allocate a struct of type ext (reserved index or TYPE_OWN_BASE + n); c must equal the type's field count. The struct's type word carries its row's flags (15.6: mutable, map, box; term.h). |
| 21 | `OP_GETFIELD` | `a=dst b=struct c=index` |  | `ra = rb.fields[c]` | Read a field; past the end of an older image's reserved struct it reads int 0, of an own struct it is badcode; nil crashes with R_NIL (15.6). |
| 22 | `OP_MKCLOSURE` | `a=dst b=captures c=ncaptures ext=func` | +ext | `ra = closure func ext{rb .. rb+c-1}` | Allocate a closure of function ext capturing registers rb .. rb+c-1. |
| 23 | `OP_TYPEIS` | `a=dst b=value ext=type` | +ext | `ra = (dynamic type of rb == ext)` | Type test: ext is a TY_* id or a struct type id. |
| 24 | `OP_BUILTIN` | `a=dst b=args c=nargs ext=builtin` | +ext | `ra = builtin ext(rb .. rb+c-1)` | Call a builtin (B_*). Two-result builtins also write ra+1. |
| 25 | `OP_CONV` | `a=dst b=src c=mode` |  | `ra = conv_c(rb)` | Integer conversion: c=0 int(rb) of an int64 (low 32 bits); c=1 int64(rb) of an int (sign-extended); c=2 uint8(rb), c=3 uint16(rb), c=4 int8(rb), c=5 int16(rb) of an int or int64: the low 8 or 16 bits, zero- or sign-extended (15.3 for c=3..6); c=6 int64(uint32(rb)) of an int (zero-extended). |
| 26 | `OP_ADD64` | `a=dst b=lhs c=rhs` |  | `ra = rb + rc` | int64 addition. |
| 27 | `OP_SUB64` | `a=dst b=lhs c=rhs` |  | `ra = rb - rc` | int64 subtraction. |
| 28 | `OP_MUL64` | `a=dst b=lhs c=rhs` |  | `ra = rb * rc` | int64 multiplication. |
| 29 | `OP_DIV64` | `a=dst b=lhs c=rhs` |  | `ra = rb / rc` | int64 division; a zero divisor crashes with R_DIV_ZERO. |
| 30 | `OP_REM64` | `a=dst b=lhs c=rhs` |  | `ra = rb % rc` | int64 remainder; a zero divisor crashes with R_DIV_ZERO. |
| 31 | `OP_NEG64` | `a=dst b=src` |  | `ra = -rb` | int64 negation. |
| 32 | `OP_EQ64` | `a=dst b=lhs c=rhs` |  | `ra = rb == rc` | int64 equality. |
| 33 | `OP_NE64` | `a=dst b=lhs c=rhs` |  | `ra = rb != rc` | int64 inequality. |
| 34 | `OP_LT64` | `a=dst b=lhs c=rhs` |  | `ra = rb < rc` | int64 less-than. |
| 35 | `OP_LE64` | `a=dst b=lhs c=rhs` |  | `ra = rb <= rc` | int64 less-or-equal. |
| 36 | `OP_BOX64` | `a=dst b=src` |  | `ra = box64(rb)` | Make rb a K_INT64 box (no-op if already boxed); an int64 inside `any` is always boxed. |
| 37 | `OP_CLEAR` | `a=first b=count` |  | `ra .. ra+b-1 = nil` | Set dead registers to nil so they stop being GC roots (b = 0 does nothing). |
| 38 | `OP_RETN` | `a=first b=count` |  | `return ra .. ra+b-1` | Return b values into the caller's registers dst .. dst+b-1, dst = the CALL's or CALLV's ra (RET returns one). |
| 39 | `OP_CALLV` | `a=dst b=closure c=nargs` |  | `ra = rb(rb+1 .. rb+c)` | Call the closure in rb with args rb+1 .. rb+c: its captures, then the args, are the callee's parameters; anything but a closure whose function takes captures+c parameters (nil) is badcode. |
| 40 | `OP_AND` | `a=dst b=lhs c=rhs` |  | `ra = rb & rc` | int bitwise and. |
| 41 | `OP_OR` | `a=dst b=lhs c=rhs` |  | `ra = rb OR rc` | int bitwise or. |
| 42 | `OP_XOR` | `a=dst b=lhs c=rhs` |  | `ra = rb ^ rc` | int bitwise xor. |
| 43 | `OP_ANDNOT` | `a=dst b=lhs c=rhs` |  | `ra = rb &^ rc` | int bit clear. |
| 44 | `OP_SHL` | `a=dst b=value c=count` |  | `ra = rb << rc` | int left shift; a count >= the width gives 0, a negative count crashes with R_BAD_SHIFT. |
| 45 | `OP_SHR` | `a=dst b=value c=count` |  | `ra = rb >> rc` | int arithmetic right shift; a count >= the width gives 0 or -1 by sign, a negative count crashes with R_BAD_SHIFT. |
| 46 | `OP_AND64` | `a=dst b=lhs c=rhs` |  | `ra = rb & rc` | int64 bitwise and. |
| 47 | `OP_OR64` | `a=dst b=lhs c=rhs` |  | `ra = rb OR rc` | int64 bitwise or. |
| 48 | `OP_XOR64` | `a=dst b=lhs c=rhs` |  | `ra = rb ^ rc` | int64 bitwise xor. |
| 49 | `OP_ANDNOT64` | `a=dst b=lhs c=rhs` |  | `ra = rb &^ rc` | int64 bit clear. |
| 50 | `OP_SHL64` | `a=dst b=value c=count` |  | `ra = rb << rc` | int64 left shift (count as SHL; the count may be either representation). |
| 51 | `OP_SHR64` | `a=dst b=value c=count` |  | `ra = rb >> rc` | int64 arithmetic right shift (count as SHR). |
| 52 | `OP_ADDF` | `a=dst b=lhs c=rhs` |  | `ra = rb + rc` | float addition. |
| 53 | `OP_SUBF` | `a=dst b=lhs c=rhs` |  | `ra = rb - rc` | float subtraction. |
| 54 | `OP_MULF` | `a=dst b=lhs c=rhs` |  | `ra = rb * rc` | float multiplication. |
| 55 | `OP_DIVF` | `a=dst b=lhs c=rhs` |  | `ra = rb / rc` | float division; a zero divisor gives +Inf, -Inf or NaN. |
| 56 | `OP_NEGF` | `a=dst b=src` |  | `ra = -rb` | float negation (flips the sign bit: -0 from 0). |
| 57 | `OP_EQF` | `a=dst b=lhs c=rhs` |  | `ra = rb == rc` | float equality (NaN equals nothing; -0 == 0). |
| 58 | `OP_NEF` | `a=dst b=lhs c=rhs` |  | `ra = rb != rc` | float inequality (true if either is NaN). |
| 59 | `OP_LTF` | `a=dst b=lhs c=rhs` |  | `ra = rb < rc` | float less-than (false if either is NaN). |
| 60 | `OP_LEF` | `a=dst b=lhs c=rhs` |  | `ra = rb <= rc` | float less-or-equal (false if either is NaN). |
| 61 | `OP_CONVF` | `a=dst b=src c=mode` |  | `ra = conv_c(rb)` | Float conversion: c=0 float64(rb), c=1 float32(rb) of an int or int64; c=2 int(rb), c=3 int64(rb) of a float, truncated toward zero, NaN giving 0 and out of range the nearest end; c=4 float64(rb), c=5 float32(rb) of a float (rounded to nearest even). |
| 62 | `OP_DIVU64` | `a=dst b=lhs c=rhs` |  | `ra = rb / rc` | uint64 division; a zero divisor crashes with R_DIV_ZERO. |
| 63 | `OP_REMU64` | `a=dst b=lhs c=rhs` |  | `ra = rb % rc` | uint64 remainder; a zero divisor crashes with R_DIV_ZERO. |
| 64 | `OP_LTU64` | `a=dst b=lhs c=rhs` |  | `ra = rb < rc` | uint64 less-than. |
| 65 | `OP_LEU64` | `a=dst b=lhs c=rhs` |  | `ra = rb <= rc` | uint64 less-or-equal. |
| 66 | `OP_SHRU64` | `a=dst b=value c=count` |  | `ra = rb >> rc` | uint64 logical right shift (count as SHR: a count >= 64 gives 0). |
| 67 | `OP_SETFIELD` | `a=src b=struct c=index` |  | `rb.fields[c] = ra` | Write a field of a heap struct of a mutable type (a pointer's target, a map header); nil crashes with R_NIL, anything else (a const or immutable struct, past the end) is badcode. |

## Builtins

Called with `OP_BUILTIN`: `ra = builtin ext(rb .. rb+c-1)`, where `ext` is the id below. Arguments are
the registers `rb ..`; a builtin with two results writes `ra` and `ra+1`.

| Id | Name | Arguments | Results | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | `B_PRINTLN` | `values...` | `nil` | Print the values, space-separated, with a newline, to the console. |
| 1 | `B_SPAWN` | `closure` | `pid` | Start a new actor running the closure. |
| 2 | `B_SELF` | - | `pid` | The calling actor's PID. |
| 3 | `B_SEND` | `pid, msg` | `nil` | Copy msg into the target's mailbox (a value that may not cross modules is R_BAD_MSG). |
| 4 | `B_RECEIVE` | - | `msg` | Block until a message arrives and take it. |
| 5 | `B_MEMORY` | - | `ProcInfo` | The calling actor's memory figures (actor.ProcInfo). |
| 6 | `B_SPAWN_LINK` | `closure` | `pid` | Spawn and link atomically. |
| 7 | `B_SPAWN_OPT` | `closure, Options struct` | `pid` | Spawn with actor.Options (MaxMemory). |
| 8 | `B_LINK` | `pid` | `nil` | Link to another actor. |
| 9 | `B_UNLINK` | `pid` | `nil` | Remove a link. |
| 10 | `B_TRAP_EXIT` | `bool` | `nil` | Turn exit trapping on or off: linked exits arrive as ExitMsg. |
| 11 | `B_EXIT` | `code` | `(does not return)` | Terminate the calling actor with an exit code. |
| 12 | `B_KILL` | `pid, code` | `nil` | Terminate another actor with a code. |
| 13 | `B_MONITOR` | `pid` | `ref` | Monitor an actor: its end arrives as DownMsg. |
| 14 | `B_DEMONITOR` | `ref` | `nil` | Cancel a monitor. |
| 15 | `B_MAKE_REF` | - | `ref` | A fresh unique reference. |
| 16 | `B_RECEIVE_TIMEOUT` | `ms` | `msg, ok` | Receive with a timeout in milliseconds; ok is false on timeout. |
| 17 | `B_SEND_AFTER` | `ms, pid, msg` | `ref` | Send after a delay; the ref cancels it. |
| 18 | `B_CANCEL_TIMER` | `ref` | `bool` | Cancel a send-after timer; true if it had not fired. |
| 19 | `B_SLEEP` | `ms` | `nil` | Suspend the calling actor. |
| 20 | `B_NOW` | - | `int64` | Monotonic milliseconds. |
| 21 | `B_CALL` | `pid, req, ms` | `reply, ok` | Request/reply with a timeout (actor.Call). |
| 22 | `B_REPLY` | `Request struct, reply` | `nil` | Answer an actor.Request. |
| 23 | `B_REGISTER` | `name, pid` | `bool` | Register a name for a PID. |
| 24 | `B_WHEREIS` | `name` | `pid, ok` | Look up a registered name. |
| 25 | `B_UNREGISTER` | `name` | `nil` | Remove a registered name. |
| 26 | `B_PORT_OPEN` | `driver string, cfg any` | `pid, ok` | Open a port driver (port.Open). |
| 27 | `B_PORT_CLOSE` | `pid` | `nil` | Close a port. |
| 28 | `B_STR_CONCAT` | `a, b` | `string` | Concatenate two strings. |
| 29 | `B_LEN` | `string \| slice \| Bytes \| Buffer` | `int` | Length of a sequence. |
| 30 | `B_INDEX` | `string \| slice \| Bytes, i` | `element` | Element i; a byte (of a string, []byte or Bytes) as an int. |
| 31 | `B_SETINDEX` | `slice, i, v` | `nil` | Store an element; a []byte stores v & 0xFF. |
| 32 | `B_SLICE` | `string \| slice \| Bytes, lo, hi` | `the same kind` | Sub-sequence; every bound is explicit, any negative or out-of-range one is badcode (a slice's hi may reach cap). |
| 33 | `B_MAKE_SLICE` | `elemkind, len, cap, zero` | `slice` | New slice; elemkind 0 term, 1 byte; every element is `zero` (0 for bytes). |
| 34 | `B_APPEND` | `slice, mode, zero, v...` | `slice` | Append. Mode 0: the terms v...; 1: the bytes v...; 2: every element of the term slice v (one v); 3: every byte of the []byte or string v (one v). Growth is decided once for all of them: if they do not all fit in cap, a new array (x2, min 4, spare slots = zero) gets them and the old one is left untouched. |
| 35 | `B_COPY` | `dst slice, src slice \| string \| Bytes` | `n` | Copy elements; n is the count copied. |
| 36 | `B_CAP` | `slice` | `int` | Capacity of a slice. |
| 37 | `B_STR_FROM` | `[]byte \| Bytes` | `string` | String from bytes (a copy). |
| 38 | `B_BYTESLICE_FROM` | `string \| Bytes` | `[]byte` | Byte slice from a string or Bytes (a copy). |
| 39 | `B_STR_CMP` | `a, b` | `-1 \| 0 \| 1` | Compare two strings. |
| 40 | `B_BUF_NEW` | `cap` | `Buffer` | New bytes.Buffer with an initial capacity. |
| 41 | `B_BUF_WRITE` | `buf, string \| []byte \| Bytes \| byte (an int)` | `nil` | Append to a Buffer. |
| 42 | `B_BUF_FREEZE` | `buf` | `Bytes` | Freeze into Bytes (a copy: heap K_BYTES up to GOGO_BYTES_INLINE bytes, else off-heap); buf is emptied and stays usable. |
| 43 | `B_BYTES_FROM` | `string \| []byte` | `Bytes` | Bytes from a string or slice (a heap copy, any size). |
| 44 | `B_BYTES_EQUAL` | `Bytes, Bytes` | `bool` | Same contents. |
| 45 | `B_BYTES_COPYTO` | `Bytes, []byte` | `n` | Copy Bytes into a slice; n is the count copied. |
| 46 | `B_PORT_HANDOFF` | `port pid, to pid` | `bool` | Hand a port's events to another actor (port.h port_handoff). |
| 47 | `B_NET_SUBSCRIBE` | - | `bool` | net.Subscribe: receive network events (port.h port_subscribe). |
| 48 | `B_CONFIG_GET` | `key string` | `value string, ok bool` | sys.Config (host->config_get; "wifi." keys hidden). |
| 49 | `B_FS` | `op int, args...` | `result(s)` | gogo/fs, run by the Vm's fs_builtin hook (actor.h; vfs/builtin.c). |
| 50 | `B_CODE` | `op int, args...` | `result(s)` | gogo/code (module_builtin, module.h; CODE_OP_*). |
| 51 | `B_UNIX_TIME` | - | `int64` | sys.Time: Unix milliseconds, vm_unix_time_ms (0: unknown). |
| 52 | `B_SET_UNIX_TIME` | `ms int64` | `bool` | sys.SetTime, vm_set_unix_time_ms (false: below the build-time floor). |
| 53 | `B_RANDOM` | - | `int` | sys.Random: an int in [0, 2^30), vm_random. |
| 54 | `B_FLOAT` | `op int, args...` | `result(s)` | (15.2, GOGO_FLOAT) gogo/math and strconv.FormatFloat / ParseFloat (float_lib, runtime/floatlib; FLOAT_OP_*). |
| 55 | `B_PRINTLNU` | `mask, values...` | `nil` | (15.3) println with unsigned values: bit i of the int mask (i < 30) marks value i a uint64 (an int64's bits), printed unsigned. |
| 56 | `B_PANIC` | `v` | `(does not return)` | panic(v): print "panic: " and v (as println prints it) to stderr, then end the calling actor with R_PANIC. Deferred calls do not run. |
| 57 | `B_CMP` | `a, b [, x [, mode]]` | `-1 \| 0 \| 1 \| 2` | A total order of two values, for == and switch on interfaces, structs and arrays: kinds first, then ints, int64s and floats by value (a NaN equals nothing; -0 == 0), Refs by serial, strings and Bytes by bytes, structs of one type field by field (a struct of a mutable type, a pointer or a map, by identity: 15.6), arrays (slices) element by element, anything else by term identity (a func, a Buffer). A third argument (its value unused) says a and b are arrays; without it a slice at the top, one held by an interface, equals nothing, itself included. Nesting past 64 levels, other than through a struct's last field or an array's last element, is badcode, and so is a compare that visits more than 65536 terms (values sharing subvalues). Does not preempt. A fourth argument (15.6, gogo/maps), mode 1 or 2, makes it a total order: a NaN equals a NaN and sorts before every other float, and a key it cannot order (a func, a Buffer, a pointer or a map at the top, or with mode 2 a slice) gives 2. |
| 58 | `B_RESERVED_58` | - | - | Kept for distributed actors (badcode until then). |
| 59 | `B_RESERVED_59` | - | - | Kept for distributed actors (badcode until then). |
| 60 | `B_RESERVED_60` | - | - | Kept for distributed actors (badcode until then). |
| 61 | `B_SPRINT` | `mode, v` | `string \| nil` | The text println prints for v, without the newline (a box as its value, a pointer's target after &, a map as map[k:v ...]): mode 0 returns it as a new string, mode 1 writes it to the console (gogo/fmt). |

## Type ids and reserved types

`OP_TYPEIS` takes a `TY_*` id for basic types, or a struct type id. Struct types use their type-table
index: the reserved types below by their fixed index, an image's own types as `TYPE_OWN_BASE` (128)
plus their position after the reserved rows (design.md §5.6, "Types"). Reserved types only grow at the
end, and only with `int` fields.

| Id | Name | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `0x10000u` | `TY_INT` |  |
| `0x10001u` | `TY_BOOL` |  |
| `0x10002u` | `TY_STRING` |  |
| `0x10003u` | `TY_PID` |  |
| `0x10004u` | `TY_REF` |  |
| `0x10005u` | `TY_INT64` |  |
| `0x10006u` | `TY_BYTES` | heap K_BYTES, off-heap handle, T_EMPTYBYTES |
| `0x10007u` | `TY_FLOAT32` | (15.2) a 2-word K_FLOAT |
| `0x10008u` | `TY_FLOAT64` | (15.2) a 3-word K_FLOAT |

| Index | Name | Fields |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | `TYPE_PROCINFO` | Memory int |
| 1 | `TYPE_REASON` | Code int, Func string |
| 2 | `TYPE_EXITMSG` | From PID, Reason Reason |
| 3 | `TYPE_DOWNMSG` | Ref Ref, From PID, Reason Reason |
| 4 | `TYPE_REQUEST` | From PID, Ref Ref, Body any |
| 5 | `TYPE_OPTIONS` | MaxMemory int |
| 6 | `TYPE_GPIO_CONFIG` | Pin, Mode, Edge, DebounceMs int: cfg of the "gpio" port |
| 7 | `TYPE_GPIO_WRITE` | Value int: gpio command |
| 8 | `TYPE_GPIO_EDGE` | Pin int, Value int: gpio event |
| 9 | `TYPE_NET_IFCONFIG` | (no fields): cfg of the "netif" port |
| 10 | `TYPE_NET_SETADDR` | IP, Mask, Gateway, DNS int |
| 11 | `TYPE_NET_UP` | IP, Gateway, DNS int |
| 12 | `TYPE_NET_DOWN` | (no fields) |
| 13 | `TYPE_NET_ADDR` | IP, Port int |
| 14 | `TYPE_NET_UDP` | Port int: cfg of the "udp" port |
| 15 | `TYPE_NET_SENDTO` | Addr Addr, Data bytes.Bytes |
| 16 | `TYPE_NET_DATAGRAM` | From Addr, Data bytes.Bytes |
| 17 | `TYPE_NET_DIAL` | IP, Port, TimeoutMs int: cfg of the "tcp" port |
| 18 | `TYPE_NET_LISTEN` | Port int: cfg of the "tcp_listen" port |
| 19 | `TYPE_NET_SHUTDOWN` | (no fields): tcp command, send FIN |
| 20 | `TYPE_NET_RESUME` | (no fields): tcp command, unpause an accepted connection |
| 21 | `TYPE_NET_CONNECTED` | (no fields): tcp event |
| 22 | `TYPE_NET_ACCEPTED` | Conn PID: tcp_listen event |
| 23 | `TYPE_FS_INFO` | Size int, IsDir bool: fs.Stat |
| 24 | `TYPE_FS_SPACE` | Used, Total int: fs.Usage |
| 25 | `TYPE_KBD_CONFIG` | RepeatDelayMs, RepeatMs int: port.Open("kbd") |
| 26 | `TYPE_KBD_KEY` | Code, Char, Mods int; Down bool: key event |

| 29 | `TYPE_POWER_READ` | (no fields): ask for a Battery now |

| 35 | `TYPE_IMU_CONFIG` | RateHz, Gestures, BatchMs int: port.Open("imu") |
| 36 | `TYPE_IMU_GESTURE` | Kind, Value int: gesture event |
| 37 | `TYPE_IR_TX` | CarrierHz, DutyPct int: port.Open("ir_tx") |
| 38 | `TYPE_IR_RX` | GapUs int: port.Open("ir_rx") |
| 39 | `TYPE_AUDIO_MIC` | RateHz, FrameMs, GainDb int: port.Open("mic") |
| 40 | `TYPE_AUDIO_SPEAKER` | RateHz, VolumePct int: port.Open("speaker") |
| 41 | `TYPE_NET_DIALTLS` | IP, Port, TimeoutMs int, Host string: cfg of the "tls" port |
| 42 | `TYPE_HOST` | Arg int, Data bytes.Bytes: cfg of a host-defined port |
| 43 | `TYPE_POST` | From PID, Kind int, Data bytes.Bytes: a host post, host-port command or event |
| 44 | `TYPE_SCREEN_CONFIG` | Cols, Rows int: port.Open("screen") |
| 45 | `TYPE_ERRORS_CODE` | the box of an errors.Code (an int) in an interface |
| 46 | `TYPE_ERRORS_ERRORSTRING` | s string: errors.New's error |

## Exit reasons

Codes 10..63 are kept for the VM; 64..99 are library failures (`R_FAILED` + a `GOGO_E_*` code); user
codes are >= 100.

| Code | Name | Note |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | `R_NORMAL` |  |
| 1 | `R_KILLED` |  |
| 2 | `R_OUT_OF_MEMORY` |  |
| 3 | `R_MAILBOX_OVERFLOW` |  |
| 4 | `R_NO_PROC` |  |
| 5 | `R_DIV_ZERO` |  |
| 6 | `R_BAD_CODE` |  |
| 7 | `R_SHUTDOWN` |  |
| 8 | `R_BAD_SHIFT` |  |
| 9 | `R_BAD_MSG` | a value that may not cross modules (msg.h) |
| 10 | `R_PANIC` | panic(v), a failed type assertion, a method call on a nil interface (15.4) |
| 12 | `R_NIL` | a nil pointer dereference, a write to a nil map: GETFIELD or SETFIELD of nil (15.6) |
| 64 | `R_FAILED` | + a GOGO_E_* code: a library failure (no VM code uses it) |

## Image file layout

Little-endian 32-bit words (`runtime/vm/image.h`; narrative in [design.md](design.md) §5.6). Images are
position-independent and run in place. Sections follow each other in this order:

| Section | Size (words) | Contents |
|---|---|---|
| header | 8 | 0 magic `0x4F474F47` ("GOGO"); 1 version `major<<16 \| minor`; 2 `n_funcs`; 3 `n_types`; 4 `consts_words`; 5 `code_words`; 6 `entry` (only validated: boot starts the `"main"` export); 7 `n_reserved` |
| functions | 3 x `n_funcs` | per function: 0 code offset (words, into the code section); 1 `nparams \| nregs<<16`; 2 name (constant offset of a string) |
| types | 2 x `n_types` | per type: field count, name (constant offset); the first `n_reserved` rows are reserved types, then the image's own |
| constants | `consts_words` | strings, int64 boxes, byte blobs and other objects, each starting with a header word |
| code | `code_words` | instruction words and their `ext` words |
| constant map | ceil(`consts_words` / 32) | one bit per constant word, set where an object starts (word `i / 32`, bit `i % 32`); read in place, no RAM |
| requirements | 1 + `n_requires` | the count, then one constant offset per name: a port driver (`"kbd"`, `"tcp"`) or a mount prefix starting with `/` |
| exports | 1 + 2 x `n_exports` | the count, then `{name constant offset, function index}` pairs; `main` is exported as `"main"` |

The loader checks the tables and the constant area (the map must mark exactly the object starts the
constant headers define; requirement and export names must be constant strings at marked starts;
function indexes in range) and refuses anything else (`IMG_ERR_BOUNDS`); a `major` other than the VM's,
or a `minor` above it, is `IMG_ERR_VERSION`. The compiler stamps each image with the lowest minor its
opcodes, builtins and reserved types need. Versioning policy and validation are in design.md §5.6.
